headline: KAIST, a South Korean science and technology university, will present its plan for physical AI at an event on 13 October, where its president is due to demonstrate a wearable robot.
score_reason: Pool score 5 lowered one point: the source headline speaks as if the vision were already declared, but the event is only scheduled for 13 October and nothing has been shown.
importance_line: It signals that KAIST, a South Korean science university, wants physical AI, meaning AI that senses and moves in the real world, to reach health care, defence and logistics as well as factories, but this is an announcement of a planned event, so nothing has been shown and the vision is the university's own.
summary: DongA Science reports that KAIST (the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology) said on 11 October it will hold "Physical AI KOREA 2026" at its Daejeon campus on 13 October, where it plans to present a physical AI strategy that goes beyond humanoid robots into healthcare, defence, logistics and daily life. President Bae Choong-sik is scheduled to wear and demonstrate a wearable robot built by Professor Kong Kyung-chul's team, and five research teams will show work including a humanoid that can carry objects heavier than 15 kilograms.
